Bioengineering Graduate Academics
The Department of Bioengineering has an active, interdisciplinary bioengineering program in conjunction with faculty from the Schools of Medicine, Health and Rehabilitative Sciences, Dental Medicine, The Graduate School of Public Health, and the clinical staffs at the UPMC hospitals in addition to the other departments within the School of Engineering.
This program is directed toward graduate bioengineering education and research, with particular emphasis on the PhD program. Its scope is broadly defined to incorporate the application of engineering principles, methods, and technology in two broad areas:
Scientific inquiries into fundamental biological phenomena
Development of instrumentation, materials, devices, and systems relative to application in the biological sciences and medicine.
Thus, the bioengineering faculty is applying various forms of engineering principles, technology, and methodology to a broad variety of medical and life sciences problems.

PhD Programs
PHD Program
The Doctor of Philosophy Program in the Department of Bioengineering emphasizes our excellence in bioengineering research and education.
Students pursuing the PhD degree are required to pass a preliminary examination based on their Bioengineering coursework at the end of their first year of graduate study. Students pursuing the PhD are also required to complete two, one-credit teaching practicums, and present a PhD proposal, ideally within 18 months or so of taking the preliminary exam. Each PhD candidate makes a final, public PhD thesis defense to fulfill the requirements for the PhD degree.

Research MS
Research M.S. Program (Thesis)
See the Bioengineering, MS Program in the Pitt catalog
The Research MS program requires a total of 30 credits, which includes:
Graduate Engineering Mathematics - 3 credits
Statistics for Bioengineers - 3 credits
Societal, Political and Ethical Issues in Bioengineering - 3 credits
Life Sciences - 3 credits
Track Courses - 9 credits
Electives - 3 credits
MS Thesis - 6 credits
Teaching Practicum - 0 credit
Bioengineering Seminar - 0 credits (must take 3 seminars)
Total - 30 credits
Other required courses may be tailored to the student's background and interests. Typically, completion of the Research MS program requires two years. The student is expected to have identified a research mentor before being admitted in the program. Within the first year of enrollment (preferably within the first semester), the MS candidate is expected to finalize the general area in which he/she will write a thesis. By the third semester of enrollment, the student is to prepare a Master's Thesis, following University requirements for Electronic Theses and Dissertations (ETDs.) The student (under the guidance of his/her advisor) selects a thesis committee of three or more persons. For MS students, the committee will need to consist of three faculty members total and at least two need to be member of the Bioengineering faculty. However, all three can be Bioengineering faculty as there is no requirement to have one member from outside of Bioengineering. The committee should consist of the student's advisor (who will act as Chairman of this committee), at least one additional faculty member from within the Department of Bioengineering and at least one faculty member from outside the Department of Bioengineering. The committee meets at least once per year and oversees the Thesis Defense.

Professional MS in Medical Product Engineering (MS-MPE)
Our Master's in Medical Product Engineering program focuses on the application of engineering innovation to identify challenges in health care through developing medical technology. The program has graduated over 200+ graduates in 10 years, and after the 1.5 years it usually takes to complete this program, we expect that you will:
Be well-positioned for career success in your areas of professional interest.
Most MS-MPE graduates prefer industry positions in start-ups or in established organizations. Some opt to pursue careers in medicine, government, research, and education. You may come in with notions of what you want to do and we will help you achieve those aspirations. Even if you change your mind, and career focus and direction, during this program, we will encourage, support and help you make that transition as well.
Understand better what impact you would like to make in the wide field of Bioengineering and health-care related fields, and an initial set of ideas and a preliminary plan to do so. We expect our graduates to make such an impact, and expect you to aspire to do so.
Pitt has contributed to the development of many impactul and historic advances in medical technology and healthcare, including:
Polio Vaccine
Kidney Transplantation
Cardio-Pulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)
Left Ventricular Assist Devices (LVADs)
Total Artificial Hearts (TAHs)

Professional MS in Bioengineering - Neural Engineering Focus
See the Bioengineering, MS Program in the Pitt catalog
Download our Professional MS in Bioengineering - focus on Neural Engineering information sheet.
Program Coordinator: Prof. Neeraj Gandhi (ms-neural@pitt.edu)
WHY STUDY NEURAL ENGINEERING AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH?
Pitt is a recognized leader in the emerging discipline of Neural Engineering. Our core faculty and clinical collaborators offer courses that prepare students to work in this exciting and dynamic field. Neural Engineering, which encompasses neural prosthetics, brain-computer interface systems, epilepsy monitoring, deep brain stimulation, engineering approaches to psychiatric disorders, and brain-inspired computation and device design, is a fast-growing field that integrates technological advances to provide clinical benefits.
The program is offered by Pitt’s nationally ranked Department of Bioengineering. Instruction will be in-person and online. The 30-credit program can be completed in 2 semesters depending on the student’s background knowledge/experience, although most students typically take three semesters.
Students will garner a deep knowledge of the biology of the nervous system, and how, from an engineering perspective, to treat disorders, build clinical devices, and develop computational models. The non-thesis program is designed to provide excellent training for a terminal degree for a research engineer position in academia or industry in Neural Engineering or related fields such as Medical Devices or Data Science, or as a stepping stone towards a PhD in these fields or medical school. Students are also required to complete an internship aligned with their career goals.
CONCENTRATIONS
Neural engineering students will pursue didactic coursework that builds core competency in at least two concentration areas. Typical areas include but are not limited to:
Brain-computer interfaces
Neural tissue interface
Neural imaging and signals
Neural devices and neuromorphic engineering
The concentrations for core competency will be selected in consultation with the program director and will take into consideration the student’s previous training and career aspirations.

Professional MS in Bioengineering - Biomechanics Focus
Students in this focus area will receive advanced training specializing in biomechanics while completing a non-thesis bioengineering graduate degree. By combining advanced understanding of bioengineering, mechanical engineering, physiology, and rehabilitation science concepts to analyze and improve human movement and describe biomechanical behavior of tissues and organs, students in this focus area will be well-equipped to pursue careers in industry, clinical laboratories, government, or pursue additional educational opportunities such as PhD programs, law school, or medical school.
Curriculum – 30 credits
By combining the below courses, students design a customized curricular plan to be completed in a year to acquire biomechanics knowledge and technical expertise to align with each student’s career goals. Each student’s program of study will be finalized with MS program leadership and track chair Spandan Maiti.

Required Internship (3 credits)
Students may pursue internships in academic, clinical, or industry settings, aligned with their individual interests and career goals. These experiences are intended to provide hands-on professional training during the MS degree, whether conducting research in a laboratory, gaining insight into the biotech industry, or working directly within a medical or clinical environment.

Be a part of our community:
Pitt Bioengineering has been a global leader in biomechanics for decades, driving real-world advances in rehabilitation and orthopedic care, including nationally adopted wheelchair and assistive technologies and widely used gait, balance, and fall-prevention approaches. Across the university, we integrate engineering, physiology, orthopedics, rehabilitation science, and sports medicine with strong clinical and translational impact through close partnerships with UPMC. Our students can study movement at the cellular, tissue, or full-body level, and combine tissue and organ mechanics research with human movement, gait, balance, ergonomics, and performance across our various classrooms and laboratories. Popular laboratories include the Human Mobility & Balance Lab (HMBL), Human Engineering Research Lab (HERL), and the Rehabilitation Neural Engineering Labs (RNEL).
Professional MS in Bioengineering - Clinical Adoption, Realization and Engineering (CARE) Focus
Clinical Adoption, Realization and Engineering, or CARE, is built on the belief that better healthcare innovation happens when engineering rigor is paired with clinical insight and human-centered understanding. For students in this focus area, our goal is to develop graduates who can recognize unmet clinical needs, work across professional boundaries, and contribute to the design, translation, and improvement of healthcare technologies and systems. The bioengineering component brings a solution-oriented mindset, while nursing brings daily exposure to patient care, clinical workflow, safety, and implementation realities. At its core, this focus area cultivates the clinician-engineer: a professional who bridges technical innovation and care delivery to design and deploy better solutions for patients and providers.
Curriculum – 30 credits
Students will design a customized plan with MS program leadership and Program Director. The coursework consists of required graduate courses in both the Department of Bioengineering and the School of Nursing.

Professional MS in Bioengineering - Molecular, Cellular, and Systems Engineering (MCSE) Focus
Students in this focus area will receive advanced training specializing in molecular, cellular and systems engineering (MCSE) while completing a non-thesis bioengineering graduate degree. Students will focus on mechanobiology, gene and protein networks, omics integration, and synthetic biology while bridging wet-lab experimentation with computational modeling, AI-driven biology, and systems pharmacology. With applications spanning cancer biology, cardiovascular signaling, immune engineering, regenerative pathways, and precision medicine, this focus area prepares students for industry roles in biotech and pharmaceutical R&D or for PhD training in bioengineering, computational biology, or systems pharmacology. Students will also be well-equipped to pursue careers in clinical laboratories and government or pursue additional educational opportunities such as law school or medical school.

Be a part of our community:
Bioengineering researchers in the MCSE track have pioneered gene regulatory network models, advanced systems biology algorithms, and led breakthroughs in pulmonary hypertension, vascular remodeling, cancer pathway mapping, and systems pharmacology. Our faculty in the MCSE track maintain strong ties to the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine’s Computational & Systems Biology program, Pitt’s Organ Pathobiology and Therapeutics Institute, and UPMC’s Hillman Cancer Center and Vascular Medicine Institute. Supported by these close collaborations, these efforts have translated systems models into precision oncology decision pathways, integrated computational biomarkers into large multi-institutional studies, and helped deliver cardiovascular therapies such as implantable blood pumps, artificial lungs, stents, and cardiac patches to patients.
Professional MS in Bioengineering - Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine (TERM) Focus
Students in this focus area will receive advanced training specializing in Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine (TERM) while completing a non-thesis bioengineering graduate degree. Creating materials, cells, and technologies to repair and regenerate the human body, TERM integrates biomaterials, stem-cell engineering, tissue engineering, and regenerative medicine into a comprehensive, translationally focused program. Students will explore extracellular matrix (ECM) scaffolds, stem-cell therapies, organoid models, tissue mechanics, and immunoengineering, while benefiting from leadership from the McGowan Institute for Regenerative Medicine, one of the world’s premier regenerative medicine centers. With strong clinical partnerships across UPMC, Plastic Surgery, Orthopaedics, and Rehabilitation, the program prepares graduates for careers in the regenerative medicine and biomaterials industries or for continued study in a PhD program.

Be a part of our community:
At Pitt and UPMC, bioengineering researchers in TERM have been pioneers in regenerative medicine, developing ECM biomaterials now used worldwide for tissue repair, implanting regenerative scaffolds in thousands of patients, advancing early tissue-engineered blood vessels and cardiac patches, conducting some of the first tissue-engineered organ transplant trials, and leading innovations in stem-cell mechanobiology as well as tissue-engineered liver and pancreas constructs. Pitt’s innovation ecosystem also allows TERM research to be easily integrated into licensed & patented startup companies for entrepreneurship opportunities.
Professional MS in Bioengineering - Additional Focus Areas
Get a professionally focused, non-thesis master’s degree in our department’s areas of expertise. To complement our existing Professional MS in Bioengineering – Neural Engineering Focus program, we now offer the following additional focus areas:
Biomechanics,
Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine (TERM),
Molecular, Cellular and Systems Engineering (MCSE), or
Bioimaging and Signals (BIS)
This 30-credit master’s program lets you design a customized curricular plan to be completed in a year by taking advanced courses and participating in hands-on experiences (including a required independent study course) to acquire domain knowledge and technical expertise that align with your career aspirations. This program is ideal for individuals seeking research/technology-related careers in industry or other settings (e.g., university-based laboratories, clinical laboratories, government research and/or regulatory organizations). This program is also beneficial to individuals planning to pursue additional educational opportunities (e.g., PhD, medical school, IP law).
Although an undergraduate degree in Bioengineering is helpful, individuals with other STEM-based educational backgrounds are welcome to apply. This program is also compatible with the EAGr program of the Swanson School of Engineering, University of Pittsburgh.
If interested, please attend one of our upcoming open houses or contact Dr. Ouahiba Boukaabar, Assistant Director of Master’s Programs (oub3@pitt.edu) to learn more about the program and the application process.

Katz Graduate School of Business and School of Engineering, positions individuals with an undergraduate degree in engineering or the hard sciences to take a management role in a company that has a significant engineering and/or technological focus.
The Department of Bioengineering and the Katz Graduate School of Business offer a dual MBA/MS program, with the following requirements. Neural Engineering in Neurosurgery
Co-directed by Aaron Batista and Jorge González-Martínez (Neurological Surgery)
This program brings together eight trainees (four postdoctoral bioengineers and four neurosurgery residents), along with 32 affiliated faculty and clinicians.
Trainees are organized into eight collaboration clusters: epilepsy, stroke, speech and language mapping, sensory restoration, pain, trauma, movement disorders, and brain tumors.
Postdoctoral fellows shadow neurosurgeons in the operating room, while residents conduct laboratory research under the supervision of an engineering mentor.
Trainees complete a required yearlong course, BIOENG 2805: Translational Neural Engineering
Research areas include thalamic stimulation for speech and motor recovery after stroke, intraoperative decision-making in tumor resection, spinal cord stimulation for chronic pain, and implantable neuromodulation systems
